idiom_name: value-returning methods with CA1806 / [Pure] / the TryParse convention
implementation_notes: C# methods return their result by convention (string.Trim returns the trimmed string, LINQ operators return new sequences) and the .NET analyzers make the do-not-ignore rule checkable: CA1806 flags unused new objects, ignored string-creating calls, ignored HRESULT or error codes, ignored LINQ results and calls to [Pure] methods, and additional_use_results_methods extends it to a team's own APIs. For 'the outcome is the interesting value' the language idiom is TryParse - a bool result plus an out parameter, so the caller cannot proceed without reading the outcome. Use [Pure] (System.Diagnostics.Contracts) to declare that a method's value is the whole point of calling it, and remember that a Task-returning method invoked and discarded hides its exceptions as well as its result.
pitfalls: LINQ is deferred: a query result that is never enumerated does no work at all, so an ignored value is a silent no-op rather than a wasted computation.
Ignoring a Task-returning method (or writing _ = Task.Run(...)) swallows exceptions along with the result; only awaiting consumes it properly.
CA1806 is a suggestion, not an error, by default (.NET 10) and must be configured per project for custom APIs, so the convention is only as strong as the build settings.
